_about: Every choice in the piece lives here: the player (js/piece.js) reads it, audition.html changes it live, and slides s3b, s4 and s16 play with it. Keys starting with _ are notes, ignored by the code.

choose._at_play: fixed: play data/piece.json. random: when play is pressed, draw three voices from data/pool.json

light._about: The light is my window switching: one soft glow per switch, somewhere on the screen. Safety limits (at most 3 pulses in any second, and a brightness change too small to count as a flash under WCAG 2.3.1) are in js/lights.js and cannot be raised from here.
light._seed: where the glows fall. null: somewhere new every time. A number: the same places every time
light._size: a glow's diameter, as a fraction of the screen's height: smallest and largest
light._edge: how soft a glow's rim is, as a fraction of its radius: 0 is a hard rim, 1 is soft all the way to the centre
light._attack: seconds a glow takes to come up
light._hold_max: a glow stays while I stay in that app, but never longer than this many seconds
light._release: seconds a glow takes to fade once I switch away
light._breathe: while a glow stays, it breathes: this many times a second (at most 3), dipping by this fraction of its brightness
light._strength: 0 to 1: how much of the safe maximum brightness change a glow may use
light._color: the colour of the light on day paper and on night paper. On day paper a light can only show as a tint, so it is a gold close to the paper's own brightness, which lets it show at nearly half strength: the safety limit is on brightness, not on colour

time._about: When each event sounds, in played seconds.
time._mode: compressed: fit the piece into 'target' seconds. realtime: play 'excerpt' seconds from 'offset' at 1:1.
time._gap_cap: in compressed mode, the longest rest, in seconds, between two events
time._entries: played second at which each voice comes in
time._exits: seconds before the end at which each voice plays its last note, so the three do not stop together. Each voice is fitted between its entry and its exit
time._tail: seconds kept free at the end of a compressed piece for the last bells to ring out

pitch._about: Also used for the MIDI file. MIDI note numbers; D minor pentatonic.
pitch._voice_roots: one register per agent, like a consort of viols: bass, tenor, treble
pitch._tool_degrees: degree of the scale a tool sounds on, within its voice's register. 'tick' is a dry percussive tick, not a pitch. Anything unlisted uses 'other_degree'.
pitch._summons_degree: the bell: this many scale steps above the voice's root, so it sits in the voice's own register but above its texture

sound._about: How it sounds. Levels are in dB; 0 is full scale. audition.html has a slider for every number here.

mix._about: prompts and bells on top, the agents' work underneath, the ticks lowest; reverb is the level of the room

sound._pan: left to right, per agent: -1 is full left

agents._about: One bowed timbre for all three agents, like a consort of viols: a soft string tone, filtered, with a swell and a little vibrato.
agents._length: a note lasts as long as its tool call did, played, but never shorter or longer than these (seconds)
agents._brightness: filter cutoff as a multiple of the note's pitch: higher is brighter, more rosin
agents._detune: a second string, this fraction out of tune, to thicken the tone

ticks._about: Shell commands: a dry wooden tick in the agent's register, not a pitch.

bells._about: Stop and Notification: a bell in the agent's own register. The most important sound in the piece.
bells._ring: seconds the lowest partial rings; the others ring for shorter
bells._brightness: 0 to 1: how much of the upper partials

prompts._about: My prompts: a warm, breathy wind tone, sparse and in front.
prompts._breath: how much air in the tone

pulse._about: The bread slide's beat: a soft, low felt drum, the steady clock the agents never have.

limiter._about: The last thing before the speakers, so that the three voices and their bells together never clip.

bread._about: The bread slide (s3b): its schedule, read from the slide itself, played in strict time. Each action is my wind tone on the beat; the waits are counted out by the pulse; the bell is the bread, done.
bread._minutes_per_beat: real minutes one beat stands for: half an hour is two beats, two hours eight
bread._longest_wait: the longest wait, in beats (the levain's night plays as this many)

exposition._about: Before the piece, each part alone: one prompt, one agent working and then summoning, one pulse of light. Then everything together.
exposition._seconds: how long each part has alone, and the silence before the piece begins
